newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt up after 30-year auction.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt up after 30-year auction.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices staged a recovery late in the day following a rebound in U.S. Treasury securities after a strong 30-year Treasury auction, emerging market traders said.
"There were worries over supply in the Treasury market, but the 30-year went okay and we are bouncing back now," said one emerging market debt strategist at a U.S. investment bank.
AT 1615 EST/2115 GMT, Argentine FRBs were 1/4 firmer at 83-5/8 bid, Venezuelan DCBs were 5/8 higher at 84-1/4 and Mexico's UMS-26 bonds were 5/8 better at 102-1/8.

Although prices slipped early in the day with Treasuries following comments by a senior Japanese Finance Ministry official that the dollar recovery was coming to an end, sources said prices made it to the plus column after the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond hit an eight-month low of 6.54 percent on strong auction results.

One source said the turbulence in the markets over the comments in Japan shows what the risks are for the markets if Japan begins to move and tighten monetary policy. But the source believes weakness in the economy will keep a tightening by the Bank of Japan on hold in the near-term.

"We think a lot of that (the comments) was noise and we don't see them moving at all. We still think the economy is relatively weak and I think the market realized that and has come back on the back of that," he said.
Meanwhile, sources said the unveiling of Mexico's 1997 budget proposal to Congress had few surprises.
"Everything that has come through so far suggests that there are no surprises," said one market expert.

"What we don't have yet is the full budget, but all the headlines on the inflation projection, the growth projection and the spending projection in real terms are in line with expectations so there is nothing to move the markets."
Elsewhere, Russian dollar-denominated Vneshekonombank loans were one percentage point higher at 78-3/4.
